title: Add integration tests for perf-canary metric label schema + cardinality
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Motivation: We’ve been iterating quickly on perf-canary attribution dimensions (model/region/gpu_sku/runtime_build, plus a few runtime-side tags) and we already saw one near-miss where an extra label would have blown up series count. This PR adds integration tests that scrape a representative canary metrics payload and enforce the label schema + a conservative cardinality budget in CI so we catch issues before they ship to prod. Scope: Adds a hermetic integration test that spins up the metrics registry with perf-canary enabled, emits a small matrix of canary requests (models x regions x gpu_sku x runtime_build), scrapes the /metrics endpoint, and validates: (1) All perf-canary metrics use an allowlisted label key set; (2) Required labels are present on canary regression KPIs; (3) No high-cardinality labels (request_id, trace_id, prompt_hash, user_id, etc.) appear; (4) Series count per metric remains under a budget for the fixture (guardrail for accidental dimension creep). Notes: This is intentionally a guardrail test, not a full correctness test of p95/tokens/sec math (that lives in the perf-canary runner repo and telemetry pipeline tests). Related: ENG-2845, and recent runtime PRs adding canary tags/exports (PR #39122, #39135, #39180).
commits: test(observability): add perf-canary metrics scrape harness
test(observability): enforce canary label allowlist + required labels
test(observability): add cardinality budget assertions and failure output
chore(metrics): unify gpu label naming to gpu_sku in canary registry
docs(testing): add guidance for extending canary label schema safely
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Love the direction. Two asks: (1) please centralize the allowlist in a schema package (so other repos/pipelines can import the same set), and (2) make the failure output actionable (print which metric + which unexpected labels).
Caleb Johnson (author): +1. Pushed follow-up: allowlist moved to telemetry/metrics/schema and test now prints per-metric offending label keys + sample series labels.

Thomas Baird (review): Can we also assert the absence of obviously dangerous labels (request_id/trace_id)? Allowlist catches this indirectly, but explicit assertions help future readers. Also: the budget threshold should be documented (why that number).

Caleb Johnson (author): Added explicit denylist checks (request_id, trace_id, span_id, prompt_hash, session_id) and documented the budget rationale in the test + docs. Budget is sized to catch accidental additions, not to model full prod matrices.
Logan Wright (review): Noticed a mismatch: fixture emits gpu_type but spec calls it gpu_sku. Please align naming and include a regression test to prevent reintroducing gpu_type.
Caleb Johnson (author): Fixed by aliasing/removing gpu_type for canary and updating exporter to emit gpu_sku only. Added an assertion that gpu_type label key is never present on canary metrics.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Question: should runtime_build be required everywhere or only for the regression KPIs? Some low-level metrics might not carry it (to reduce overhead).
Caleb Johnson (author): Good call. Required-label assertions are now limited to the KPI set (p95 latency + tokens/sec + request counters) and we only enforce allowlisted labels for the rest.
Allison Grant (approval): Looks good now. Failure messages are clear and schema is centralized. Approved.
Thomas Baird (approval): Approved. Thanks for adding the explicit denylist and the doc note on budget sizing.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved. Naming alignment to gpu_sku is exactly what we need for cardinality control.
